Multiple Vulnerabilities in NGINX Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
item.description: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in NGINX, the most severe of which could allow for remote code execution. NGINX is software used for web serving, reverse proxying, caching, and load balancing. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could result in remote code execution. Depending on the privileges associated with the account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
item.description: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.
